affectedPublicSurfaces: THE RUN STATUS VOCABULARY, which is a wire contract in three languages at once. `services/agent/status.py::WorkflowRunStatus` has exactly seven members (`queued`, `running`, `waiting_approval`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `failed`); `packages/contracts/src/agent-events.ts` mirrors them as the const array `WORKFLOW_RUN_STATUSES` backing `export type WorkflowRunStatus`; and `services/agent_runs/listing.py::RunListItem` exposes `status` (and `stop_reason`) on `GET /demo/runs`, while the SSE stream at `GET /demo/runs/{run_id}/events` carries the same vocabulary on its payloads. Adding `waiting_external` widens what a seller's client can receive on BOTH surfaces — a client with an exhaustive switch over the union will see a state it has never seen.

TWO Postgres CHECK constraints, not one. `models.py::WorkflowRun.__table_args__` declares `ck_workflow_runs_status` (`status IN ('queued','running','waiting_approval','completed','cancelled','timed_out','failed')`) AND `ck_workflow_runs_stop_reason` (a sixteen-value IN list). Adding the state touches the first; adding `external_wait_expired` touches the second. Both live in the model AND in a migration, and both must move together or the model/migration parity test catches the drift after the fact instead of before.

THE ACTIVE-RUN PARTIAL INDEX — a consequence the issue does not name and the executor must decide deliberately. `uq_workflow_runs_active_shop_product` (re-keyed by #1701) filters on `postgresql_where="status IN ('queued','running','waiting_approval')"`. A run parked in `waiting_external` is NOT in that set today, so it would silently stop holding its subject's active-run slot — which would let a second run start on a subject a suspended run still owns, and would quietly undermine #1710's cross-workflow subject lock before it is even written. Decide it in this slice, state the decision in the PR, and prove it.

`NON_TERMINAL_STATUSES` and the reverse-totality test. `status.py` names `frozenset({QUEUED, RUNNING})` as EXACTLY the statuses no `stop_reason` can target, and `tests/unit/test_workflow_run_status_mapping.py` asserts that shape in both directions. `waiting_approval` is targeted by `paused_for_confirmation`; `waiting_external` therefore needs its OWN suspending stop reason. THE ISSUE NAMES NONE — its only new reason, `external_wait_expired`, is the reaper's TERMINAL cause and lands in a terminal status. Meta must name the suspending reason (an analogue of `paused_for_confirmation`, within `String(32)`) or the reverse-totality assertion in acceptance criterion 1 cannot pass; adding `waiting_external` to `NON_TERMINAL_STATUSES` instead would be a different and wrong decision, because that set means 'pre-stop', not 'suspended'.

`TerminationPolicy` (`services/agent/playbooks/base.py`) gains `external_wait_timeout_h`, defaulting to None = this workflow may NOT wait externally. `OPTIMIZE_PRODUCT_TERMINATION_POLICY` (`max_iterations=6`, `max_extensions=1`, `extension_iterations=2`, `wall_clock_timeout_s=300`, `approval_timeout_h=4`, `required_steps=("update_product_listing","update_product_price")`, `terminal_tools=("conclude_without_changes",)`) keeps `external_wait_timeout_h = None`, so `optimize_product_2` cannot enter the state and its behaviour is unchanged by construction. The reaper (`workers/tasks/reaper.py`, beat entry `reap-abandoned-workflow-runs`, `*/5`) judges an externally-waiting run ONLY by that field, never by `approval_timeout_h`.

NOTHING RESUMES THE STATE IN THIS SLICE. `resume_agent_workflow` still has exactly one caller — `api/routes/agent_runs.py::_enqueue_resume_agent_workflow`, invoked from `submit_confirmation_decision`. The webhook consumer is #1708. A run that enters `waiting_external` here can only be reaped, and that is the honest, intended shape.

The dual-language half additionally needs the node toolchain and `packages/contracts`' dependency graph installed, because `tests/unit/test_agent_events_contract.py` shells out to `node -e` and `require("typescript")` — without it, it fails with a bare CalledProcessError rather than skipping, which reads as a product defect. migrationCompatibility.notes: ONE ADDITIVE, EXPAND-ONLY migration that WIDENS two CHECK constraints and drops nothing. `ck_workflow_runs_status` gains `'waiting_external'`; `ck_workflow_runs_stop_reason` gains `'external_wait_expired'` (21 chars, inside `String(32)`) and the suspending reason Meta names. A widened IN-list accepts every value it accepted before, so the PREVIOUS release keeps writing and reading `workflow_runs` unchanged — it simply never emits the new values. No column is added, dropped, renamed or retyped; there is no backfill and no NOT NULL. The same two constraint texts also live in `models.py::WorkflowRun.__table_args__` and must move in the SAME commit, or the schema-parity test finds the drift after the fact. If the active-run partial index's WHERE clause is widened to include `waiting_external`, that index change rides this same migration and is called out separately in the PR — it changes which rows collide, which is a behaviour change wearing a schema change's clothes. The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. The chain's single head today is `055_juli_app_sync_state_update` (revising `054_juli_app_bronze_select`), but W6 and W8 both hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause` and `043_juli_app_role`, chained one after the other) from exactly this mistake.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. `WorkflowRunStatus` keeps its seven members, the reaper keeps one timer, `TerminationPolicy` has no external-wait field, and no run can wait on anything but a person for four hours. Clear Excess and Replenish stay blocked, which is the pre-existing state the ladder names. Nothing is exposed, nothing is partially applied, no data hazard.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the previous release FIRST and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker: the previous code neither writes nor recognises `waiting_external`, so it runs correctly against the widened CHECK and needs no downgrade. Only if the schema must ALSO be reverted, `alembic downgrade -1` narrows the two CHECK constraints back — and that downgrade MUST FAIL LOUDLY with an explicit named error, never silently delete or coerce a row, when ANY `workflow_runs` row has `status = 'waiting_external'` or `stop_reason = 'external_wait_expired'` (and, if #1701's schema is being reverted in the same operation, when any row carries a non-product `subject_type` or a NULL `product_id`). Narrowing a CHECK under live rows would otherwise either fail opaquely at constraint validation or tempt an operator into deleting suspended runs. Both refusals are asserted PRE-MERGE, not discovered in production. Order: previous code first, downgrade second, so no live process is mid-write against a constraint being narrowed. A run left in `waiting_external` across a code-only rollback is inert: the previous reaper does not recognise the state and will not reap it, so drain or reap those runs deliberately before narrowing.
